title: Blog Content Package v0.3
description: One draft blog post for one platform, ready for a human to publish. v0.3 makes the platform first-class: `platform` names it, `platform_metadata` carries exactly that platform's own fields, `content_intent` records the search intent, `overlap` records how the post relates to what already exists on either platform, `quality.layers` separates structural, semantic, evidence and platform-fit quality, and `lineage.prompt` names the prompt, profile, standards and schema versions with the digests of the requests sent. Every v0.2 field keeps its meaning. v0.1 and v0.2 rows stay valid against their own schemas and read as Naver packages; this is a new version, not a reinterpretation. The runtime never publishes: `published_url` is written back by the operator.

then.description: A package cannot claim to be published without the URL — that URL is the only input the ranking tracker has, and a `published` state without one silently ends the feedback loop.
A naver package carries naver's metadata only, and its URL is a naver post's.
A tistory package carries tistory's metadata only, and its URL is a tistory post's.

platform.description: Where the post is for. Chooses the profile that wrote the request, read the answer, measured it and rendered the paste (`runtime/mvp_runtime/blog_platform.py`).

target_keyword.description: The one keyword this post is written to rank for. Exactly one, deliberately: a draft targeting three keywords ranks for none, and the ranking tracker needs a single subject.

content_intent.description: The search intent: `keyword_intent` read off the keyword by a fixed lexicon (blog_overlap.INTENT_MARKERS), `declared_intent` what the draft's own brief declared (null where the platform asks for no brief).

selection_evidence.description: How the target was chosen. Candidate rows are the SELECTION brief's; none of their numbers describe the target unless the target is one of them, and a reader must take target numbers from `target_evidence` only.

ad_competition.description: Naver Search Ad `compIdx` — ADVERTISER BID competition, not blog difficulty. Recorded for the operator; never a selection gate.

queue_score.description: The vault queue's score for this candidate (demand weighted by reach), when the seeds came from the queue.

seed_source.description: Where the seeds came from: the schedule's request (`request`) or the vault keyword pipeline's queue (`vault_queue`, with the queue's date, how many candidates it listed, and how many were skipped as already written).

section.description: Which part of the queue the seeds were read from: Naver's '다음 편 후보' sections, or the '티스토리 전용' section a Tistory fire reads (optional; absent on rows written before 2026-10-05's second Tistory change).

target_evidence.description: The research run on `target_keyword` itself (the content run's own brief). `status: missing` means that brief carried no row for the target — the numbers are then ABSENT, never another keyword's. Missing is not zero.

matched_keyword.description: The row's keyword as the venue spelled it (Search Ad strips spaces), matched to the target by normalized equality.

ad_competition.description: Naver Search Ad `compIdx` — ADVERTISER BID competition, not blog difficulty. Recorded for the operator; never a selection gate.

blog_competing_posts.description: Naver's count of blog documents matching the target — the target's alone, never a sum across keywords.

trend_points.description: Relative search interest, normalised to the peak of the requested window. Comparable within this array only — never across packages.

lineage.description: The runtime traces this package came from. Real trace ids of governed runs, or null where that run did not happen (an operator override has no selection research; a draft that passed first time has no revision).

prompt.description: Which prompt produced this package, by version and by digest: a version names what was intended, the sha256 the bytes actually sent. A revision that did not run has no digest.

title_candidates.description: Alternatives for the operator to choose from, not a ranking. Each should carry the target keyword near the front.

body_paste.description: The body exactly as it should be pasted into the platform's editor. Naver: plain text, paragraphs separated by blank lines, NO markdown — SmartEditor ONE does not interpret it, so '##' and '**' would land in the post as literal characters; formatting intent lives in `body_blocks`. Tistory: markdown the runtime itself wrote around the draft's plain paragraphs (headings, the table, internal links, the reference list).

body_blocks.description: What to do to the pasted text in the editor, addressed by paragraph index. The split between this and `body_paste` is the whole point of the two-file output.

tags.description: Naver caps a post at 30 tags; the same ceiling holds for Tistory.

image_shots.description: Screens for the operator to capture — not generated images. Posts about using an AI tool need the tool's actual screen; a generated illustration reduces trust and, repeated across posts, becomes a tell.

alt_text.description: The image's alt text (Tistory): one sentence describing the screen, not a keyword list.

sources.description: The draft's cited sources that resolved to evidence the producing run actually had ([S#] search hits, [K#] keyword rows; mock fixtures excluded). A reference the run never saw is dropped, not kept on trust.

fact_checks.description: Statements the operator must verify before publishing — prices, free-tier scope, usage limits, feature availability, policy, versions, dates, API availability. Flagging is not verifying: the runtime emits only `needs_manual_verification` (no resolvable source) or `source_cited` (a source this run had — a place to check, not a check). `verified` exists for a human's later record and requires the source and the time.

quality.description: The draft's measurement against the lane's standards and what the one automatic revision did. `needs_edit` is a state for a human, never a reason the package was withheld; neither state publishes anything.

revision_detail.description: When the one revision was blocked: the governed run's own block message (which provider failed and how), so the reason survives past the lane's outer code. When the revision ran but was further from the standards than the first draft (REVISION_FURTHER_OFF:KEPT_FIRST_DRAFT): what the revision missed.

brackets_inserted.description: How many brackets (a missing object opener or missing closers) the final draft's JSON was missing and had put back before it parsed (blog_draft.repair_brackets). Absent when none were needed; the draft's text is never changed.

layers.description: Quality in four layers, never one number. Only `structural` gates (its failures are `failures` above, which decide `quality_state`); the other three are advisory and never change the review state. `semantic` is deterministic proxies (`method`), and the judgements no proxy can make honestly are `not_measured` — no LLM judge runs.

overlap.description: How this post relates to what already exists on either platform (vault posts and ledger packages), classified deterministically by `runtime/mvp_runtime/blog_overlap.py`. Every match carries its reason and the action the platform's policy took; `decision` is the most severe. `source_state: unavailable` means the existing posts could not be read — no match then is not 'no overlap'.

platform_metadata.description: Exactly one key: the package's platform, holding that platform's own fields. A Naver package is never made to carry Tistory's fields, nor the reverse.

naver.description: Naver's own fields: the paste is SmartEditor ONE plain text.

tistory.description: Tistory's own fields (Google/Daum search). `meta_description` is DERIVED from the body's first 400 characters, because Tistory has no description field and writes that text into <meta name=description> itself (`meta_description_source` says so); it is a preview of what search will show, not a field to fill.

internal_links.description: Links to the same blog's posts, each resolved to a candidate the runtime listed ([L#]); a link the list did not hold is dropped.

publish_state.description: `draft` until the operator publishes and returns the URL. The runtime never sets this to `published` on its own — it has no way to observe a publish it did not perform.
